description: The formal CDSS application process, orientations, and the physical plant inspection.

sections.title: Mandatory Orientations
sections.summary: Complete the required CDSS training components before final submission.

bullets.label: Complete Component I (Online)
bullets.detail: This is a general overview of the licensing process. You must print and save the certificate of completion for your application packet.

bullets.label: Attend Component II (Live/Virtual)
bullets.detail: This is a detailed, category-specific orientation for ARFs. It covers Title 22 regulations in depth and allows you to ask questions to licensing staff.

sections.title: Part A & Part B Application
sections.summary: Submit the core legal and operational documents to the Centralized Applications Bureau (CAB).

bullets.label: File LIC 200 & Application Fee
bullets.detail: The primary application form. Fees for ARFs vary based on capacity (e.g., 1-6 beds or 7-15 beds). Fees are non-refundable.

bullets.label: Submit Part B (Operational Plan)
bullets.detail: This includes your Program Design, LIC 309 (Admin Organization), and LIC 401 (Financial Plan). This is where you prove you can run the facility.

bullets.label: Attach LIC 999 (Disaster Plan)
bullets.detail: Must include specific evacuation routes, emergency contacts, and transportation plans for residents with varying ambulatory statuses.

sections.title: Pre-Licensing & Fire Clearance
sections.summary: The final hurdles before the license is issued.

bullets.label: Request STD 850 (Fire Clearance)
bullets.detail: Licensing will trigger this request to the State Fire Marshal. You must ensure all R-3.1 fire code requirements are met before they arrive.

bullets.label: Pass the Pre-Licensing Inspection
bullets.detail: An LPA (Licensing Program Analyst) will walk through the home to verify that everything in Part A and B matches the physical reality of the site.
